_comment: Model H — Hindi. Architecture is identical to the other language's by design: both Phase 1 vocabularies are 16,000, so nothing forces them apart, and holding shape constant makes the corpus the only variable in the H-vs-L comparison. Keys beginning with '_' are documentation and are ignored by ModelConfig.from_json.
_vocabulary: 16,000, from the Phase 1 SentencePiece BPE model at hindi/tokenizer/hi.model. Verified byte-identical to the copy in the Drive artifacts, and round-trips held-out text with zero unknown tokens.
_parameter_budget: 24,298,176 trainable parameters against the assignment's ~25M target. The token embedding is 7,168,000 of that — 29.5%. A 32,000 vocabulary would have spent 14,336,000 here and left far less for depth, which is why the smaller vocabulary is worth its slightly higher fertility.
_depth_vs_width: 448 x 7 gives an aspect ratio (d_model / n_layer) of 64.0, the same as GPT-2 small's 768/12. Alternatives at the same budget were 384 x 10 (24.09M, aspect 38.4) and 512 x 5 (24.22M, aspect 102.4). The 512 variant is too shallow to compose much; 384 x 10 is a reasonable deeper option but costs more sequential layers per step on a single T4 for no measured gain at this scale. 448 divides evenly into 7 heads of 64, the width at which attention kernels are efficient.
_positional_scheme: Learned absolute. Chosen over sinusoidal or rotary for being fully explainable end to end, and because a learned table makes the context ceiling explicit: there is no row to look up beyond position max_seq_len, so the model simply cannot be run on a longer sequence.
_norm_placement: Pre-norm. The residual stream stays an unbroken identity path from embeddings to final norm, so gradients reach early layers without traversing a normalisation. Post-norm at this depth needs a far more carefully tuned warmup.
